title: Water as a Right: Sheinbaum Reports Recovery of 5 Billion Cubic Meters
author: Fernanda Monroy
content:
_This article by[Fernanda
Monroy](https://contralinea.com.mx/author/fermonroy/) originally appeared in
the [September 1, 2026 edition of
Contralínea](https://contralinea.com.mx/interno/semana/agua-como-derecho-
sheinbaum-reporta-recuperacion-de-5-mil-millones-de-metros-cubicos/), a
leading Mexican investigative journalism magazine._

More than **5 billion cubic meters of water have been recovered from private
concessions** following the **reform to the National Water Law** —an amount
sufficient, according to President **Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo** , **to supply
more than 90 million people for a year.**

During the presentation of her Second State of the Nation Report, the
President explained that the reform, published in December 2025, changed the
way the federal government conceives of water resources: **water ceased to be
treated as “a commodity” and came to be recognized as a human right and a
resource belonging to the nation.**

She also recalled that for decades water was subjected to a logic of
privatization that had profound consequences for the country. “We have spoken
a great deal about what the privatization of energy resources meant for the
country, but with water, turning water into a commodity had extremely serious
effects.”

**As a result of the reform** , she detailed, the federal government granted
**12,346 concession titles to communities** , as well as to small and medium-
sized producers. Some municipalities, she said, also regained direct access to
the resource through the National Water Commission (**Conagua**).

Among the cases mentioned by the President were Mexicali and Tijuana, whose
municipal governments now hold direct concessions from Conagua, whereas
previously they had to pay private parties for water.

According to the President, the change seeks to ensure that access to water no
longer depends on private interests and returns to its status as a right.

### Cleaning Up Rivers and Recovering Water

President Claudia Sheinbaum stated that, in addition to recovering
concessions, her administration is working on measures to **clean up and
restore some of the rivers most affected by pollution and environmental
deterioration.**

In a first stage, she reported, **work is under way on the Atoyac, Lerma-
Santiago, and Tula rivers** , where **23 treatment plants and 282 kilometers
of collector pipelines are being built and rehabilitated**. Work is also being
done to clean and dredge riverbeds, along with the construction of public
spaces in these areas.

**In parallel** , she noted, cleanup efforts are being carried out on the
**Tijuana River in Baja California; the Nogales River in Sonora; and the La
Sabana River in Guerrero.**

The goal, the head of the federal executive explained, is for water policy not
to be limited to bringing water to cities, but also **to allow the recovery of
bodies of water and to address the conditions that for years have worsened
pollution and scarcity.**

Likewise, she reported that the strategy includes the **modernization and
technification of agricultural-irrigation infrastructure across more than
250,000 hectares** , distributed among 19 irrigation districts in 15 states.

She noted that this intervention has a dual purpose: to increase agricultural
productivity and to free up water for human consumption. Improving irrigation
efficiency means using less water to obtain greater production while, at the
same time, having a larger volume available for other uses.

### Infrastructure to Guarantee Supply

**In addition to recovering and cleaning up the resource, Sheinbaum Pardo
reported that the federal government is promoting 17 strategic projects**
intended to guarantee the human right to water and to reduce the risk of
flooding.

Among them are the **200 kilometers of completed trunk networks of Healthy
Water for La Laguna** , in Coahuila, as well as the **Eastern Zone Plan for
the State of Mexico** , which, according to the President, is 40 percent
complete.

Also under way, at the same percentage of progress, is the **Comprehensive
Plan for the Metropolitan Area of the Valley of Mexico**.

She also highlighted work on the **El Novillo Dam** in Baja California Sur;
the **Campeche Acuaférico water system** ; the second line of the Guadalupe
Victoria aqueduct in Tamaulipas; a new aqueduct for the city of Colima; the
**Tunal II Dam** in Durango; the Coatzacoalcos aqueduct in Veracruz; and the
El Peaje–San José aqueduct in San Luis Potosí.

In Acapulco, she explained, the **“Acapulco Is Transformed With You”** program
includes drinking-water, drainage, sanitation, and flood-prevention works.
**Meanwhile, in Tabasco, protection works against such events are under way.**

She also announced projects about to begin, among them the **Mujer Solteca
Dam** , to supply the city of Oaxaca; a desalination plant for Tijuana and
Rosarito; a system of wells for Hermosillo, Sonora; and the **Water for
Guanajuato** and **Water for Zacatecas** projects.

Likewise, Sheinbaum Pardo reported that, with resources coordinated among the
three levels of government, **24,000 drinking-water and drainage works have
been carried out in 2,183 municipalities across the country** , aimed at
improving the daily life of communities.

In this sense, the reform and the works presented by the President form part,
according to her administration's assessment, of a change in the State's
relationship with water resources. The aim, the President argued, is for water
to once again serve the population and for its access to be guaranteed as **a
right, not as a commodity.**
